correctness.rationale: The complete three-round type recursion is derived from equality and adjacency patterns. For h>=3 and b>=2, N>2b+4 makes the 00 pattern universal, and tree uniqueness of common neighbors determines the remaining bits; the four pointed rank-two types are realized at every height. For h=0,1,2, explicit structural radius, independent-triple and 2-domination formulas distinguish exactly the five other cases. The 15-node bound is the smallest member of the collapsed stable class. Two actual code programs check representative signatures and local pattern formulas but are not used to prove infinitude.

value.rationale: The sharp six-class classification of the natural full-branching tree family detects exactly where a three-round first-order observer loses both height and degree information without a root or ancestry. The optimal smallest-representative bound is 15; an explicit rank-four neighborhood-twin separator proves that branching loss is a genuine depth-three boundary. This supplies a substantive, natural complete bounded-depth finite-model-theory benchmark rather than a computation on an arbitrarily selected small graph.
